abstract: Full-duplex speech models execute dense model inference for every audio frame throughout a live interaction. This uniform framewise schedule creates sustained GPU load across dialogue states whose computation has strong, reusable temporal structure. ReFrame formulates full-duplex inference as a silence-aware computation problem. Mutual Silence Speculation (MSS) operates when both participants are silent: it evaluates multi-frame Temporal continuations, verifies text and hidden-state stability, and applies batched Mimi audio-token correction. Listening Frame Folding (LFF) operates while the user speaks and the agent listens: it processes already-arrived user frames through parallel Temporal execution and frame-batched audio-token generation while accepting only the verified prefix. Frame-Budget Reinvestment (FBR) assigns the released frame intervals to resumable external retrieval and language-model workers, then injects timely references through Moshi's conditioning interface. We instantiate ReFrame on five full-duplex models spanning Moshi-family, phase-structured, and flattened autoregressive generation. Across the complete 1,225-conversation FDBench, ReFrame reduces measured GPU execution time by 18.80-31.01% and retains 96.92-100% non-PAD text agreement on five different models. On HaluEval tests, FBR increases the number of correct generated spoken answers from 86 to 205 under the same auxiliary-service budget. ReFrame turns recurring dialogue structure into lower inference cost and higher end-to-end service capability.

oneSentenceThesis: ReFrame 针对全双工语音模型每帧都做稠密推理的问题，用双方静音时的推测执行和用户说话时的折叠并行来省 GPU 时间，并把省出的帧预算用于可恢复的检索与语言模型查询，在 1225 段对话上省 18.80-31.01% 执行时间并保持文本基本一致。
originalTitle: ReFrame: Silence-Aware Compute Reclamation for Full-Duplex Speech Models
readerTitle: 静音时省算力、听人说话时并行算：ReFrame 如何复用全双工对话的沉默结构
